truth: a write with no permission check on a target earlier in the SAME method WARNs (the global
OPERATOR_WRITE map of the user is not a target check, B763 §763.2 residual); a check in another
method, or after the write (on a later line or later on the same line), guards nothing. --strict makes the WARN fail.

class A extends BWebServlet {
  void doPost(WebOp op) {
    CsrfUtil.verifyCsrfToken(op.getRequest());
    if (!op.getUser().getPermissions().has(BPermissions.OPERATOR_WRITE)) return;
    target.set(prop, v, op);
  }
  void late(WebOp op) {
    target.setDouble(prop, 1.0, op);
    if (!target.getPermissions(op).hasOperatorWrite()) return;
  }
  void check(WebOp op) { target.getPermissions(op).hasOperatorWrite(); }
  void other(WebOp op) {
    target.set(prop, v, op);
  }
  void same(WebOp op) { target.set(prop, v, op); target.getPermissions(op).hasOperatorWrite(); }
}
